title: Request for Datalink Availability on North Atlantic Tracks after Repeated Log-On Failures
abstract: Operator reports that controller-pilot datalink log-on fails or drops on oceanic entry, forcing voice relay and costing preferred track allocations on its long-sector ZEPHYR-24 operation.

sections.request: We fly our ZEPHYR-24 aircraft on sectors that put us into oceanic airspace for two to three hours, and the datalink is the thing that decides whether we get the track and the level we planned for. What we are seeing is that the log-on either fails outright at the boundary or connects and then drops within the first thirty minutes, after which the crew is back on high frequency voice and we are handed whatever is left. Our crews say the failure is silent: nothing tells them the connection has gone until the controller calls. The avionics shop finds no fault on the ground. We need the datalink to stay up for the whole oceanic segment and we need the crew to be told immediately when it does not.
sections.background: The problem appeared when we started using these aircraft on the oceanic network in early 2025 and it has grown with the number of sectors. Fourteen log-on failures and twenty-two mid-segment drops were logged in the first quarter of 2026. Our MRO has swapped antennas, re-terminated the coaxial run and replaced two routers with no change. Two of our competitors on the same routes with a different avionics standard do not report the same picture, which is why we believe this is a build standard issue rather than an installation issue.
sections.expected_outcome: A continuous datalink connection for the full oceanic segment on at least ninety-nine flights in a hundred, an unambiguous flight deck indication when the connection is lost, and a maintenance report that tells our shop what actually failed rather than a generic router message.

type_data.business_justification: Loss of a preferred oceanic track costs the operator between 380 and 900 kilograms of fuel per sector and, on the westbound rotation, occasionally a crew duty extension. Thirty-six datalink events in one quarter across eighteen aircraft is judged unsustainable for a network that is planned around datalink availability.
